summary: The run did not demonstrate the intended transfer sequence. A START pulse occurred at about 10 s and again at 300 s, and STOP occurred at about 120 s, but the controller only entered the fill state (active_state/controller.activeState = 1, controller.mode = 2) and never reached any wait, transfer, or drain phase. Inlet command opened from about 10.1 s to 120.1 s and again from about 300.1 s to 600 s, yet inletValve.flowSignal, tank1.inflow, tank1.outflow, tank2.inflow, tank2.outflow, transferValve.flowSignal, and drainValve.flowSignal all stayed at 0 for the full 900 s. Tank 1 high level never became true (controller.highLevelTank1 and highLevelTank1.y stayed 0), while both low-level switches stayed true throughout, so no fill completion, 10 s waits, transfer to Tank 2, or drain of Tank 2 actually occurred. At 600 s SHUT returned the controller to idle (active_state/controller.activeState = 0, controller.mode = 1) rather than opening transfer and drain until both tanks were empty; transfer and drain commands remained 0 throughout. Overall, the real trajectory shows command pulses and inlet-open indications, but no liquid movement and no completion of the brief’s required sequence.
issues: Tank 1 never reached its High-level switch: controller.highLevelTank1 min=max=final=0 and highLevelTank1.y min=max=final=0, so the required transition from filling to the first 10 s wait never occurred.

The first 10 s wait after Tank 1 high level was never entered. The event trace shows active_state/controller.activeState changed only 0 -> 1 at 10.1 s, 1 -> 6 at 120.1 s, 6 -> 1 at 300.1 s, and 1 -> 0 at 600 s; no additional phase corresponding to wait, transfer, second wait, or drain was reached.
No transfer to Tank 2 occurred. transferValve.openCmd, controller.transferOpen, transferValve.flowSignal, transfer_valve_command, and transfer_flow_report all had min=max=final=0.
No drain of Tank 2 occurred. drainValve.openCmd, controller.drainOpen, drainValve.flowSignal, drain_valve_command, and drain_flow_report all had min=max=final=0.

No liquid movement occurred anywhere in the model despite inlet-open commands. tank1.inflow, tank1.outflow, tank2.inflow, and tank2.outflow all had min=max=final=0, and inletValve.flowSignal and inlet_flow_report also had min=max=final=0.

STOP pause/resume did not resume an interrupted later phase because the process never advanced beyond filling. The trace shows STOP at about 120 s moved active_state from 1 to 6, and START at about 300.1 s returned it from 6 to 1, resuming fill only.

SHUT behavior required by the brief was not achieved. At about 600 s, active_state/controller.activeState went to 0 and controller.mode went to 1, while transfer and drain commands remained 0 for the entire run; therefore SHUT did not open transfer and drain paths until both tanks were empty.

The required reported tank-level behavior was not demonstrated. The provided results include switch signals and flow-like signals but no changing tank levels; with zero inflow and outflow throughout, the sequence based on reaching level switches could not be validated.
assumptions: The model-generation stage explicitly retained a signal-flow abstraction instead of introducing continuous tank mass/level balances or hydraulic topology, because the brief did not specify equations, geometry, capacities, or detailed flow paths.

Simulation settings were assumed for executability: StartTime=0 s, Tolerance=1e-6, Interval=0.1 s, START pulses at 10 s and 300 s, STOP pulse at 120 s, SHUT pulse at 600 s, and controller scanPeriod=0.1 s.
Tank initial levels were assumed to be 0.
Valve nominal flows were assumed to be 0.
Switch values were assumed fixed constants for executability: highLevelTank1=false, lowLevelTank1=true, and lowLevelTank2=true.

The stage explicitly stated that, because nominal flows are zero and switch values are constants, the executable model does not represent a validated physical transfer trajectory; it only preserves discrete sequence intent, STOP pause/resume behavior, and SHUT priority logic.

A further assumption implied by the parameterization is that valve-open commands do not themselves create any nonzero material flow; with all valve flow signals and tank flow connectors remaining at 0, the model effectively assumes disconnected or zero-capacity transport paths in practice, regardless of command state.
root_causes: Tank 1 never reached high level because the generated model had no physical filling behavior. Even when inletOpen/openCmd went to 1 from about 10.1-120.1 s and again from about 300.1-600 s, inletValve.flowSignal stayed 0 and tank1.inflow stayed 0, so Tank 1 had no mechanism to accumulate liquid and drive highLevelTank1 true.

The sequence stalled in fill because the transition condition out of fill depended on Tank 1 high-level detection, and that signal was hard-wired false by assumption (controller.highLevelTank1/highLevelTank1.y always 0). With that condition never satisfied, the controller could not enter the first 10 s wait, transfer, second wait, or drain phases.

Transfer never occurred because the controller never reached the post-fill transfer state, and the model also provided no nonzero transfer flow path. As a result controller.transferOpen and transferValve.openCmd remained 0, and transferValve.flowSignal remained 0 throughout.

Drain never occurred for two reasons visible in the trajectory and assumptions: the controller never reached the post-transfer drain phase, and the SHUT implementation in this executable run did not command drain open despite the brief’s intent. Therefore controller.drainOpen and drainValve.openCmd stayed 0, so drainValve.flowSignal and tank2.outflow also stayed 0.

STOP/resume only cycled between fill and paused-fill because resumeMode captured an interrupted fill state (controller.resumeMode changed from 1 to 2 at about 120.1 s) and the process had never advanced beyond fill before STOP. The later START at about 300.1 s therefore returned to mode/state 2/1 rather than any later sequence stage.

SHUT returned the controller to idle at 600 s because the model’s discrete SHUT logic, as actually simulated, drove active_state/controller.activeState to 0 and controller.mode to 1 immediately on the SHUT pulse. Since there was no liquid inventory and no implemented nonzero transfer/drain actuation under SHUT in the run, the intended empty-both-tanks behavior could not manifest.

The lack of reported tank-level progression is a direct consequence of the chosen abstraction: by preserving only signal-flow logic, fixing switch states, and setting nominal flows to zero, the model removed the continuous state variables needed to show levels rising or falling. Without dynamic level states, the brief’s level-based acceptance behavior cannot be demonstrated by this trajectory.
